latest_release.body:
# CrossWatch v0.14.8

**Release:**
A refreshed Events view, easier log sharing, more reliable episode matching, linked Silo identities and a simpler Ask CrossWatch setup.

## ✨ Highlights
- **New Events view:** Titles is now the default, with one row per title, covers and the result for every destination. 
  - Sync activity and runs now live in Events too. Wauw....its amazing.
- **Easier Ask CrossWatch:** Google Gemini is now the default with a free model filled in.
- **Silo identities:** Silo admins can now add profiles from other Silo accounts on the same server in Identities.
- **Episodes matched by ID:** MDBList, Plex, Silo, Tofa and Kodi now match episodes by their episode ID first.
  - Shows that are numbered differently, like anime in TVDB or TMDB order, now land on the right episode.
- **New Logs view:** Browse sessions alongside raw logs, with easy copy and download options for support.

**Upgrade notes:**
- **Silo:** Ratings now use Silo’s 1–10 scale, which needs a Silo server from 2026-11-17 or newer. 
- **Events:** The first time Events opens, older events are sorted by title in the background. This only takes a moment. 

## 🔧 Fixes & Improvements
- **Added:** Events Titles view shows each title once per sync run or watch, with where it went and where it failed.
- **Added:** Successful sync writes are now recorded per title, up to 500 per destination per run.
- **Added:** Events Runs view and a Sync activity heatmap, replacing the Sync activity window.
- **Added:** Title detail in Events with the path of a title, where it comes from and earlier activity.
- **Added:** WeTrakr history now uses episode IDs, building on WeTrakr’s new TVDB episode ID support.
- **Added:** MDBList history, scrobbles and progress now send episode IDs.
- **Added:** Silo Identities can include profiles from other Silo accounts, marked as Account.
- **Added:** Silo watcher picks up plays from linked accounts when a route uses identities.
- **Added:** Log sections for Sync, Watcher, Captures, Backups, Audits and System, with links from capture and backup activity.
- **Added:** Full or filtered log exports with optional version and session details.
- **Added:** Admins can set log storage from 10 MB to 10 GB. The setting survives restarts and protects pinned and active sessions.
- **Improved:** Log layouts across all themes and mobile, with a clearer Storage & retention panel.
- **Improved:** Events filters now sit in the search bar, apply instantly and support from: and to:.
- **Improved:** Events works better on phones, with a filter sheet and larger touch targets.
- **Improved:** WeTrakr interactive sync handles rejected and already added episodes per item.
- **Improved:** MDBList matches episodes by episode ID, so titles in a different season layout are no longer sent again on the next sync.
- **Improved:** MDBList history now reports episodes that MDBList rejects instead of skipping them silently.
- **Improved:** Events statistics includes captures, backups, audits and separate ratings.
- **Improved:** Silo sync and Interactive Sync search need fewer lookups, using the IDs Silo now includes in its catalog.
- **Improved:** Ask CrossWatch sends less data per question and answers in the background.
- **Improved:** Ask CrossWatch shows clearer error messages and failures now show up in the log.
- **Improved:** SIMKL watchlist picks up status changes made on SIMKL itself.
- **Improved:** Stale token protection now also covers Silo, Tofa, Kitsu, FlickList, Scrob, BingeBase and identity logins.
- **Improved:** Plex cloud history and Plex ID lookups are remembered between runs, so they need far fewer requests to Plex.
- **Fixed:** Emby and Jellyfin no longer mark the wrong episode as watched when an episode carries its show's id.
- **Fixed:** Plex cloud list sync no longer fails completely when one title is missing from Plex Discover.

detail.readme:
# CrossWatch **CrossWatch (CW)** tracks what you watch through Watcher and syncs your watchlists, ratings, history, playback progress and collections across supported media servers and trackers. **Watcher doesn't need Plex Pass or Emby Premiere.** Set up multiple Watcher routes for your servers and users, and sync pairs between media servers, between trackers, or from a server to a tracker. CW runs locally, with a web UI and a CLI to manage it all.

⭐ Star this repository to get updates


## Why CW? **Watcher doesn't need Plex Pass or Emby Premiere.** Set up multiple routes for your servers and users, and send playback activity to their chosen supported destinations. You can also keep media servers in sync with each other, connect them to trackers, or sync between trackers. Choose what each pair syncs: watch history, playback progress, watchlists, ratings or collections, depending on provider support. Run pairs manually or on a schedule. Manage it all from one place: accounts, Watcher routes, syncs, current playback and a combined watchlist. Profiles keep your setup separate from those of friends and family. Keep your data with you, without being tied to one tracker. Sync it across the services you use and keep local snapshots in the CW Tracker. When you need more control, Interactive Sync lets you review changes before applying them. The Analyzer helps you check missing items, and saved mappings let you fix wrong matches, anime episode numbering, and split or combined episodes for future syncs. ## Features - Watcher with multiple routes for different servers and users. **No Plex Pass or Emby Premiere needed.** - Server-to-server, server-to-tracker and tracker-to-tracker sync, where supported. - Watchlists, ratings, history, playback progress and collections. Rewatches too, for supported trackers. - Multiple accounts, separate profiles and managed users who can handle their own pairs, routes and schedule. - Interactive Sync to review additions, updates and removals before applying them. - Webhook scrobbling for supported providers. - Custom mappings for wrong matches, anime IDs, and split or combined episodes. - A local CW Tracker with snapshots of your server and tracker data. - Optional AI help: ask CrossWatch advice with your own AI model. It can suggest. You can also give AI apps like Claude, Codex or Cursor read-only access. Off until you set it up. ## Supported integrations CW works with Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Silo, Tofa, SIMKL, Floppy, FlickList, Trakt, WeTrakr, AniList, MyAnimeList (MAL), Kitsu, TMDb, MDBList, PublicMetaDB, PunchPlay, BingeBase, Scrob, Tautulli, Tracearr, Kodi, Nuvio, Stremio and its own local CW Tracker. Not every integration supports every feature. Some sync lists and history; others report playback activity. Setup details are in the [wiki](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/). ## Installation The examples below use Docker. See the [installation guide](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/getting-started/installation) for more details. ### Docker Compose Save this as `compose.yaml`: ```yaml services: crosswatch: image: ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest container_name: crosswatch ports: - "8787:8787" environment: TZ: Europe/Amsterdam volumes: - crosswatch_config:/config restart: unless-stopped volumes: crosswatch_config: ``` Change `TZ` to your timezone, then run this from the same folder: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` ### Docker run Or run it directly from Bash: ```bash docker run -d \ --name crosswatch \ -p 8787:8787 \ -v crosswatch_config:/config \ -e TZ=Europe/Amsterdam \ --restart unless-stopped \ ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest ``` Both examples store persistent data in a Docker volume mounted at `/config`. Keep that volume when replacing or updating the container. ### Your first sync Open [http://localhost:8787](http://localhost:8787). If Docker is running on another machine, use that machine's address with port `8787`. 1. Connect the accounts you want to use. 2. Create a sync pair: choose which services to connect and what to sync. 3. Run the pair and check the results. Use Interactive Sync if you'd like to review changes before applying them. 4. Add a schedule if you want it to run automatically. See the [first-time setup guide](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/getting-started/first-time-setup) for the full setup. ## Scrobbling **Watcher** reports playback from Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, Silo, Tofa, Kodi and Scrob to supported trackers. No Plex Pass or Emby Premiere needed for Watcher. You can also use **webhooks** from Plex, Emby and Jellyfin. Anime ID mapping is available for Watcher and webhooks with supported providers. ### Kodi The [CrossWatch for Kodi add-on](https://github.com/crosswatch-app/kodi-addon) reports playback and household viewers. It also supports ratings directly in the add-on. Set up a Watcher route per viewer and they each get their own history, even when sharing a Kodi profile. ## Mappings Sometimes the same episode has a different number on another service, or a title gets matched to the wrong movie. You can correct titles, IDs, seasons and episodes, then save the mapping for future syncs. Split and combined episodes are supported, and you can import or export your mappings. Anime ID mapping, powered by AniBridge and animeApi, supports AniList, MyAnimeList, Kitsu, SIMKL and CW Tracker pairs. ## Tools Use the **Analyzer** when something hasn't synced as expected. You can compare snapshots, find missing items and watch time differences, fix wrong matches, check pending retries and release blocked items. | Tool | What you can do | | --- | --- | | Editor | Inspect, add or block items, manage saved mappings, and handle split or combined episodes. | | Sync topology advisor | See your sync routes and spot overlapping paths. | | Playback Progress Manager | View and edit unfinished playback sessions across providers. | | Import and Export | Import tracker files or export your data. | | Events and Logs | Look through sync history, investigate problems, and filter logs by pair or run. | | Captures | Roll back provider watchlists, ratings and history. | There's also a unified watchlist, a player card showing what's playing, and notifications for sync progress and pending reviews. Schedules can be simple or configured per pair. For Plex, you can import history for removed items into your CW Tracker. ## Backup and recovery Use **Backup & Restore** to back up CrossWatch (including mappings, blocks and custom anime rules), selected CW trackers and saved captures. Save locally, with an optional copy to Nextcloud/WebDAV or a mounted folder. Schedule automatic backups, follow their progress and restore saved data from the same dialog. Recover one tracker as a new instance, or restore only mappings and blocks, custom anime rules or saved captures. Mount optional backup storage at `/backups`, or set `CW_BACKUP_ROOT` to another absolute path inside the container. ## Running without the web UI Add `-e CW_CLI_ONLY=1` to the Docker command, or `CW_CLI_ONLY: "1"` under `environment` in Compose. The API, CLI, webhooks and auth callbacks keep working. ## Memory allocator The Docker image runs CW with jemalloc, memory used during a sync is returned afterwards. To use the default Python allocator instead, add `-e CW_ALLOCATOR=default` to the Docker command, or `CW_ALLOCATOR: "default"` under `environment` in Compose. ## Run once and exit For cron, Kubernetes CronJobs or another external scheduler, use `run-once`. Set up your accounts and sync pairs first: ```bash docker run --rm \ -v crosswatch_config:/config \ -e TZ=Europe/Amsterdam \ ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest \ run-once ``` Use the volume that contains your existing configuration. If you set up CW with Compose, its volume name normally includes the Compose project name; replace `crosswatch_config` above with that volume's actual name. To run specific pairs, use their IDs, numbers or unique prefixes. Replace the example IDs below with your own: ```bash docker run --rm \ -v crosswatch_config:/config \ ghcr.io/cenodude/crosswatch:latest \ run-once --pair pair_07c3 --pair pair_91ab ``` The command exits with `0` on success and `1` if the sync reports errors or cancellation. Add `--fail-on-unresolved` if you also want unmatched items to fail the job. ## Help and feedback Setup docs are in the [wiki](https://wiki.crosswatch.app/). For questions and discussion, there's [r/CrossWatchApp](https://www.reddit.com/r/CrossWatchApp/) and the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/c9cjzHGve). Please report bugs in [Issues](https://github.com/cenodude/CrossWatch/issues), with steps to reproduce them and what went wrong. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before sending a PR. For security reports, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). The license is in [LICENSE](LICENSE). ## Support and sponsors

Every cent donated through Buy Me a Coffee goes directly to the **ALS Foundation in the Netherlands**.

Thanks to our sponsors for supporting CW.
